data.text: General A lvl advice before my memory fails me. First of all to my batchies, congrats on finishing A levels! I really hope all the best for us as we step into a new season of life — be it uni apps, retaking, or exploring other options! I hope all of us continue to live our lives meaningfully and know that you are worth so much more than a piece of paper. To my juniors/ people giving another shot at A lvls, here is some encouragement + tips from a weak student that eventually scored straight As. Combi: BCME Prelims: CDDE/B Actual: AAAA/A I have never gotten an A throughout my entire JC life so it really surprised me to see As on my report. My chem was never higher than a D, bio was always a fail, math and econs never higher than a C. I have heard that usually the grade inflation from prelims to A lvls is around 2 grades, but I want to let you know that it is possible to improve significantly by 5 grades. What did I do: Prayed damn hard for God to create miracles in my life, and he delivered. Reflect after each paper: Make sure to do your corrections properly and write down areas of improvement to act on for the next paper. Compile challenging questions with annotations into a photo album/ google doc, especially for subjects like chem and math. Social media detox: I deactivated and deleted all my social media accounts the months leading up to A levels. Sometimes it really is the damn phone. I realised that so much time could’ve been spent productively when I had no social media. Fix your sleep schedule: I never realised how important sleep was until I started sleeping at least 7 hours a day leading up to A lvls. I felt like I could think so much clearer and have less brain fog during the day. Be extreme. Don’t be afraid of doing too much if not you’ll regret doing too little. It may feel unfair that your friend doesn’t have to study as much/ do as many practice papers as you to get the same grade but you need to do what you gotta do to secure that A. Obviously I do not encourage burnout so please plan your revision ahead of time. I would even say to start doing some tys in june/july. Just ask for help: Please open your mouth and ask your friends and teachers for help. It may feel intimidating but I am sure that most of them will be willing to sacrifice some of their time for consults/ answering your questions. Be sure to ask early, but also know that it’s never too late. If you have the financial means to, tuition can help too. However, if you don’t find the tuition helpful just drop it and find another one, do not buy into the sunk cost fallacy. Be resourceful: My GP knowledge really came from free resources like JCstarterpack, Substack, Medium, Instagram, Tiktok, Telegram (before my social media cleanse). If you know friends from other schools, do ask them for their exam reviews (NYJC has amazing comments for chem tys, RI’s internal examiner’s review for econs is super detailed, VJC and Dunman econs r great too) What I wish I would’ve done: Start early. I know it’s intimidating to start tys without understanding the whole syllabus yet but I think it helps to do a few papers as early as possible. (This is for J2 peeps, J1 relax). Don’t treat it as a waste if you did it early, you can always redo the paper a few weeks later anyways. Set higher expectations for mid terms and prelims. I was really just trying to pass and survive but I realised that if I tried to aim higher, I probably would have subconsciously tried harder to do well. Get a copy of your syllabus and start blurting everything you know about each topic on a piece of paper. Review what you have missed and train your long term memory. I only did this a few days before bio papers but I think it was helpful. submitted by [link] [comments]

data.text: alevel story. I just received my alevel results, thought this wld help juniors in j1/2 that want a gauge! I'm from one of the high tier JCs, scraped in to the sch thanks to HMT (aka bottom 1%). I was constantly doing really badly since J1 despite actually studying hard for it. Can't deny i had a lot of leadership commitments that may have distracted me, but i finished my lectures and work on time, yet my grades always proved otherwise. I take 4H2s and got a whopping EUUU/C (17.5rp) for promos - my other tests pulled me up so i cld promote almost on the dot I really spent dec hols and jun hols trying to get my foundation right and you think that wld make me improve... MYES was a whopping DSUU/D (23.75rp); prelims was another whopping EESU/D (31.25rp). Yes, i was doubting how i'd do in the end of As when my prelims looked like this. and i'm surprised i didn't give up LOL. the final stretch study break is VERY important please make a schedule! I finished my whole TYS. and yes for transparency i had tuition fr chem and gp which made me qn why i still did badly throughout and i just believed it was the school papers that were difficult since i could do decent/better in TYS. I don't think my suspicions were wrong tho i know i shouldn't blame the sch when it's my lack of ability to excel. It's giving, since others in ur sch can why cant you... but yk there's always the not so smart ones in good schools😅 was definitely one of them and shit was stressful, peer pressure was so bad. I always hated getting back results bc i was accustomed to not doing well. At the end, i received ABBB/B for A levels (63.75rp), 64.5rp if i moderate using HCL. My expected grades which i counted after each paper using answer key was BBBC/B, so i predicted my RP pretty accurately. I more than doubled my RP from prelims and was genuinely happy with my grades. So if you're failing, don't give up hope, don't let your prelim grades put you down. there's still a chance :) side note: was also quite sad i couldn't really celebrate my grades bc the ppl around me didn't hit their expectations despite them doing btr than me or them being smarter than me. kind of made me feel like my grades were a fluke and ppl didn't believe i cld get what i got bc i didnt usually do well. anyone feels this way too... submitted by [link] [comments]

data.text: Over $240k, luxury watches, cars seized in anti-vape blitz; 5 arrested. Luxury watches and three cars were also seized in the anti-drug blitz. SINGAPORE – Five Singaporeans were arrested in an anti-drug operation by the Central Narcotics Bureau (CNB) on Feb 25 and 26, with almost 1,300 e-vaporiser pods seized, among others. In a press release on March 2, CNB said four men and one woman were arrested for suspected drug offences, with 1,284 vape pods and nine vapes believed to contain etomidate were seized. Cash amounting to $243,451.35, a small amount of foreign currencies, luxury watches and three vehicles - including a Ferrari car - were also seized, it added. A 36-year-old man was restrained and arrested near Bedok North in the evening of Feb 25, after he “put up a violent struggle”, CNB said. The bureau also seized 50 vapes, believed to contain etomidate. Later in the day, CNB officers arrested a 29-year-old man at the junction of Sembawang Road and Mandai Avenue. He was then escorted to a self-storage unit near Woodlands Close, where 1,084 vapes believed to contain etomidate were seized. The man’s vehicle was also seized, CNB said. Around the same time, its officers raided a residential unit near the Miltonia Close executive condominium in Yishun and arrested a man, 37, and a woman, 29. In the unit, officers found 145 vape pods, nine vapes believed to contain etomidate, cash totalling $243,451.35, small amounts of foreign currencies and luxury watches, the statement read. It added that two vehicles belonging to the man were also seized. In the early hours of Feb 26, CNB officers raided another residential unit near Woodlands Drive and arrested a 19-year-old male. Vape-related products, including five vapes believed to contain etomidate, were seized from the unit, CNB added. Investigations are ongoing. submitted by [link] [comments]

data.text: 2026 CS Summer Internship Search....redpill, tips and some encouragement. welcome all, cs kids or not. As I landed an offer for this summer'26 recently i wanted to share some tips on how to navigate through this crowded market with summer offers being the TOUGHEST to land. I would like to add that this guide is NOT for first rodeos because 3 months stints are tough to find especially without a network. Before i begin i will share more of my current credentials for a gauge of where my portfolio is at: I am a Year 2 CCDS major ontrack to grad may'28, second lower (idgaf abt school sorry), >=3 internships in various SMEs and Startups not in SWE roles, ~1.5 YoE. Mostly reached out to MNCs and Startups from oct'25, pivoting to SWE. Landed summer offer in a fintech MNC doing SWE via the firm’s University Recruitment Programme, uncredited. I do not have a network to tap on. Okay so now the tips. Start Early By far the biggest tip I received this season. I started reaching out from October but even that was late. Sometimes companies collect resumes months before winter and contact candidates going into Summer. The job i got was one I reached out to in October for a role not indicated for Summer but they contacted me in end Jan for Summer. My company did not open roles publicly for this Summer. Also worth mentioning I put clearly in my resume that I’m looking for Summer 2026 positions — my interviewers double checked with me on this. Checking job listings weekly from July onwards is good. Target MNCs and University Recruitment Programs The only companies risking a 3 month hire on an entry level are MNCs. Most SMEs that got back to me (reached out to <10) look for at least 6 months. This time I did NOT want to take another LOA so I could only target those with structured summer programmes, which many MNCs offer. It will be good to hold a list of them to keep track of routinely when they open. Prepare Early If youre targeting MNCs, passing the OAs are definitely a given and OAs are usually the hardest to pass which means starting on the DSA grind is unavoidable. Getting your resume through to the OA is the hard part — everything else after relies on the preparation you have done for it. Its a hard pill to swallow yes but 90% of the work is done before your resume is even sent out. Trust and detach yourself from the outcome I believe that best work is done when you fully detach yourself from the results. The grind, the amount of work, the preparation — when done — will eventually pay off. I dont know who needs to hear this but before I got my offer i questioned myself time and time again when i would get my big break and if I would even get one. I would break down at times because it felt like i was pivoting into a career path that was bigger than myself. If you know you have put in the work and are struggling the same way, I assure you there is light at the end of the tunnel. The technical interviews were the easiest part of the process — you just have to trust yourself with every stage and kill it. I'm not sure if these are some of the most generic advices I have given but im here mainly to give some hope to those out there still searching. During my search I found the world especially cold and rough, i wouldnt have got through it without the kindness of the people around me (if uk who u are!). This also isnt my first rodeo with increasing my surface area of luck as I've found a summer internship in Year 1 before and that was also crazy....so with my experiences accumulating, I wholeheartedly believe that if you put in the work, you can increase your surface area of luck to recreate it everytime. Your work will eventually pay off. I wish everyone the best of luck in your search, peace out! submitted by [link] [comments]
